jobs/ofr-compilations/output/texts/EO_5692.txt (August 24, 1931): 'the description of the Aiea Military Reservation be, and the same is hereby, amended to read' with new bounds. Hawaii reservation; held edges EO 6630 and EO 8320 amend the description and do not end it. B30 open supported.

jobs/wikisource-texts/output/texts/EO_1215.txt (June 17, 1910): transfers to the War Department the naval reservation 'in the City of Cebu', 'excepting that a site therein ... suitable for the storage of five hundred tons of coal shall remain under the control of the Secretary of the Navy to be used for naval purposes, and that the Navy Department shall have the unrestricted use of the wharf'; and transfers the naval reservations 'at Isabela de Basilan and Polloc, Mindanao' to the War Department. The B20r basis says the 1947 agreement 'retained the use of bases at this member's place', but by the doctrine's own list Annex B names Mactan Island, not the City of Cebu, and neither annex names Basilan or Polloc. The open lead is still right because the Cebu coal-storage site and wharf use stayed naval (the B20n class, reserved by sec. 10(b) and Note V), while the Basilan and Polloc parts are Army reservations at non-retained places (B20 class).
correct_lead: open, on B20n (naval coal-storage site and wharf at Cebu outside the bases), with the Basilan and Polloc parts disclosed as B20-class Army reservations ended no later than 1952-03-26
